findings.fix: One registry now owns routing, power registration and concurrent terminal retirement for both slots and all three providers. Worker-scoped registry injection has no ownership of process-wide bridges/rotor. Production defaults to the actual routed registry; ordinary disposable workers cannot retire it. Power attachments/readiness are cached by radio and selected through the existing native radio_id, preventing another slot's connect/disconnect from replacing the active sample context. Existing output ownership/release/selection fences and module-idle veto are retained.
findings.tests: Four new tests: both agents receive the exact worker capture gate and every slot/provider rejects connect/control after worker shutdown (including idempotent repeat); connected fake TCI closes with no controls; fake FLEX owned Tune is released while passive slot only stops transport; selected radio power context survives the other slot's attach/detach and rejects late detached-source callbacks. Reused existing fake transports; no physical/LAN/credential operations.
findings.verification: `XLOG_PORTABLE_ONLY=1 swift test --scratch-path .build/prototype-tests --no-parallel --filter 'StationRadioRegistry|Native.*Power|WorkerTerminal|LiveFlexSession|LiveTCISession|LiveStationMethods'` PASS XCTest84 plus SwiftTesting16/3 suites. Swift compile/link includes the worker. `git diff --check` PASS. Initial compiler shadowing error and new fixture's disallowed documentation-network address were corrected; actual private-LAN validation was preserved, with the accepted address reaching only an injected fake.
findings.limits: No real transmitter, provider watchdog, packaged EOF, OS shutdown or installed UI proof. Actual direct-agent release transport was not operated; its existing owned-release path is now reached through the correct actor and ownership tests remain green. Worker still awaits other service retirements in its existing order; stalled-provider/forced-termination acceptance is separate. Last accepted native selection governs the single normal-QSO power scope; radio sources cannot mix.
